intro: Somewhere between two stations that no longer exist, the night train stopped. When it started again, every ticket had been replaced with a puzzle.
echo: Agatha Christie booked a murder on the fastest train out of Istanbul.

puzzles.title: Terminus Approaching
puzzles.flavor: Not a single letter on the page, and yet it says something.
hints: Which short words are most common in English? Could any of them be hiding here?

puzzles.title: Night Mail
hints: Each jumble is almost a word from this round, but with a letter to spare. Which letter, every time?

puzzles.title: Platform Nine
puzzles.flavor: Typed in the dark, with one hand resting a key out of place.
hints: Every letter is close to the right one. Close on what? Look down at your hands.

puzzles.title: Rolling Stock
hints: The strips are alphabetised, not in order. The word lengths say where the breaks fall. Which strip could start the sentence?

puzzles.title: Last Call
puzzles.flavor: Pairs of numbers pencilled in the margin.

blocks.text: Somewhere between two stations that no longer exist, the night train stopped. When it started again, every ticket had been replaced with a puzzle.

hints: The first number in each pair never goes past the number of words on the page. What does the second count?

puzzles.title: Leaves On The Line
puzzles.flavor: Through the wall: bursts of knocks, always in pairs.
hints: Always two numbers, never more than five. How would two prisoners spell through a wall with a 5×5 grid?

meta.title: Meta: The Night Train
meta.flavor: Every report is signed with a single initial. Blaise would know what to do with them.
hints: Blaise de Vigenère needed a key to open this. Has every answer signed its work?
